newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bull aims for "significant" profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Bull aims for "significant" profit rise.

text.p: French computer company Bull said it was targeting a "significant" profit rise in 1997 after a 23 percent increase in 1996 to 376 million francs.
"Bull looks to the future with confidence and plans to show renewed sales growth in 1997," it said in a statement.

The restructuring of its personal computer activities and electronic cards should halt their losses and allow the businesses to be used as levers for higher sales growth, it said. Those businesses generated 4.4 billion francs in 1996, compared with a restated 1995 turnover of 5.9 billion.
In its systems and services activities, Bull aims for growth outpacing the overall market. Turnover from those activities rose to 19.92 billion francs from 18.61 billion.
"The group in 1997 will pursue its effort to reduce non-wage costs," it said.
